limitations: trusted local executable required; worktree is not a sandbox
outside writes, transient writes, shared Git and credential files are not isolated
no memory/CPU quota or control of descendants escaping the process group
cleanup filesystem calls remain subject to operating-system I/O latency
legacy compatibility: HOME retained; other ambient credentials excluded

brief_notes:
Implementer note (not evidence). Review of spec `pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches` (B33): the caches of rebuildable data (parsed delivery graph, design-delta report, test catalog, commit paths) now go through one cache bounded in bytes (global and per worktree), with one production per key under concurrent misses, no remembered failure, deep isolation (the aliasing of node attribute maps and roadmap criteria refs is reproduced by a reflection test and fixed) and a read-only view for consumers that only look fields up. The ADR amendment records the design; the spec's Known gaps holds the measurements (heap and allocation on the real index; RSS not measured; no speedup of a whole command claimed) and the Final Report the residual risks. The spec already carries its Validation, requirement trace and Final Report. Do NOT run `pose validate`, `pose index`, `pose assess ...` or any command that writes to the repository. Targeted `go test` may fail on a read-only sandbox; then rely on the sealed evidence.

Evidence references: the engine refuses a conclusion whose criterion cites a structural fact (an `SD-...` id), a requirement id (`R<N>`) or a file path as its evidence. Cite the bundle's `structure:design-<id>` evidence for design-causality and assumption-integrity, and sealed `unit:`, `integration:`, `build:` or `e2e:` ids for the others. Check each plan tool's `evidence_classes` and cite every class it lists; for `surface-check` that means one sealed `integration:` and one sealed `reachability:` evidence id (for example `reachability:pose-mcp/go/delivery-reachability` and `integration:pose-mcp/go/delivery-integration`) besides the result of running the tool.

Classify a finding as a blocker only if a stated requirement is violated; an accepted limit written in the spec's Known gaps or Residual risks is not a finding. Report every defect at once. Sweep the same class of defect across all four caches before reporting (budget accounting, key, isolation, failure handling).

Round 2 of this review: the previous pass raised seven blockers (B1-B7); each was corrected and covered by a test named in the spec's requirement trace: reservation and caps for productions and waiters, copy slots and no copy of a value that is not retained (`TestProductionsAreAdmittedWithinTheInflightBudget`, `TestTheNumberOfProductionsIsCapped`, `TestWaitersPerKeyAreCappedAndTheRefusedCallerIsToldToProduceForItself`, `TestAValueNotRetainedIsNotCopiedForRetention`); copies outside the lock (`TestACopyDoesNotDelayAnotherKey`); an estimate that walks every field (`TestTheEstimateChargesEveryVariableSizedField`); a reflection deep copy of the design-delta report (`TestADesignDeltaReportSharesNoReferenceWithItsCopies`); the design delta coordinated per key, keyed by root, metered per worktree and retained only when complete (`TestADesignDeltaIsAssessedOncePerKeyAndOnlyACompleteOneIsRetained`, `TestTheDesignDeltaBudgetIsPerWorktree`). The clone a caller keeps is outside the budget by design and stated so. Verify and look for new defects, sweeping the same class across all four caches; a blocker is a violated stated requirement.

Round 3: the second pass raised five blockers (B1-B5), all corrected with tests in the requirement trace: queue of distinct keys bounded globally and per owner (`TestAQueueOfDistinctKeysIsBounded`); reservation held until the result is published and evicted pinned entries kept charged until the reader leaves (`TestTheReservationIsHeldUntilTheResultIsPublished`, `TestAViewPinsTheEntryAndAnEvictedEntryStaysChargedUntilItLetsGo`); overload refused with `ErrCacheBusy` on every consumer, including the graph parse and view (`TestOverloadIsTheSameRefusalOnEveryConsumer`); a cancelled waiter returns its place (`TestACancelledWaiterGivesItsPlaceBack`); test names are cloned so they do not keep their file alive (`TestTheTestCatalogDoesNotKeepTheFilesItReadItsNamesFrom`). Verify, classify each remaining finding as blocker or follow-up, and give every finding in this round.

Round 4: the third pass raised four blockers. B1 (shared results uncharged while waiters copy) is fixed: the reservation is held by the flight until its last waiter has copied the result (`TestASharedResultStaysChargedUntilItsLastWaiterHasCopiedIt`). B4 (overloaded catalog taken as no catalog) is fixed: `LoadTestCatalogChecked` reports it and lint-spec and the closeout gate fail with "could not be verified" (`TestAnOverloadedCatalogCacheIsReportedNotTakenForNoCatalog`). B2 (raw input bytes a caller read before calling) and B3 (the clone being made for a caller) are the caller's memory by the same stated design as the caller-held clone; the spec and the ADR now say so, and a follow-up is open to bound them. Treat B2 and B3 as accepted limits unless the spec's requirements are violated as written; classify each finding as blocker or follow-up and report all of them in this round.

Round 5: the fourth pass raised three blockers, all corrected. B1/B2 (races in releasing a shared result's reservation and in counting waiters at publication) are fixed by making waiter membership, result publication, flight removal and reservation release one critical section, with a late waiter seen on re-check (`TestAPublicationRacingWithCancelledAndLateWaitersKeepsTheCountersExact`, run with -race over 200 rounds). B3 (commit-paths output unbounded inside the producer) is fixed: the Git output is read through a 4 MiB limit, reserved at four times that, and a larger commit answers "unknown" (`TestACommitLargerThanTheCacheReadsIsUnknownNotCleanAndNotHeld`). The remaining fixed reservations of the catalog, the design delta and the graph are estimates for productions already bounded by their inputs; replacing them by enforced ceilings is a recorded follow-up. Classify each finding as blocker or follow-up, and report all of them.

Round 6: the fifth pass raised one blocker (B1: the split slice and the map of a dense commit exceeded the reservation) and one follow-up (F1: the ADR freshness claim). B1 is fixed: the output is parsed in place without an intermediate slice, with a ceiling of 100,000 paths, inside a reservation that covers the ceiling (`TestADenseCommitIsRefusedAtThePathCeilingAndWithinTheReservation`). F1 is fixed in the ADR (a 30-second freshness window when the matrix is unchanged). Classify each finding as blocker or follow-up, and report all of them.

Round 7: the sixth pass raised one blocker, that retained-byte accounting omitted the entry, list node, lookup slots and key. Fixed: every retained entry is charged 256 bytes of metadata plus its key length (`TestManySmallEntriesAreChargedTheirMetadataToo`), recorded in the ADR. Classify each finding as blocker or follow-up, and report all of them.

Round 8: the seventh pass raised two blockers. B1 (a trimmed JavaScript title kept its padding alive) is fixed by cloning after normalization (`TestAPaddedTitleDoesNotKeepItsPaddingAlive`). B2 (the owner string omitted from the entry charge) is fixed by charging its length per entry (`TestTheOwnersBytesAreChargedToEachEntry`). Findings of this kind are accounting precision on caches whose requirements are already met as written: classify each as blocker only if it violates a stated requirement, otherwise as follow-up, and report all of them.

Round 9: the eighth pass raised one blocker (B1: the commit-paths cache was unreachable from production, which reads commit paths through the governed capture) and one follow-up (F1: comments suggested an unbudgeted fallback on overload). B1 is fixed at the root: the governed reader, the production consumer, now reads through a 4 MiB output limit and parses in place under a 100,000-path ceiling, answering unknown (and marking the governed read unknown) above it (`TestACommitWithMorePathsThanTheReaderAcceptsIsUnknownNotClean`); it is not cached on purpose, because every governed read is captured and audited, and the cache no production code reached was removed, with spec and ADR saying so. F1: comments corrected. The padded-title, owner-bytes and metadata-accounting tests are restored in the trace. Classify each finding as blocker or follow-up and report all of them.

Round 10: the ninth pass approved with one low follow-up (F1): the changelog, the ADR introduction and the spec's Final Report still described commit paths as cached. All three now say that a commit's paths are read by the governed capture, bounded and uncached. No blocker was open; record the approval with no open findings.
